To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temporal and spatial distribution pattern of CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells and B cells in acute and chronic distemper encepalitis lesions is in line with the hypothesis of a heterogenic immune-mediated plaque pathomechanism in distemper enecephalitis.

(1) CDV infection induces an immune response in the CNS, (2) CDV antigen expression was reduced in chronic demyelination plaques, (3) CD4+ and B cells were found in perivascular inflammatory infiltrates of chronic lesions, and (4) CD4+ T cells and B cells might be involved in the pathogenesis of chronic demyelinating distempe encephalitis.
1. CDV antigen was found at intralesional sites of all distemper encepalitic cerebella.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemical identification of T cells in the brain in dogs with spontaneous distempt encephalitis (DE).
the identification and localization of CD4+and CD8+ T cells as well the detection of B cells in the brains of dogs with spontaneous canine distemper encepalomyelitis (DE).
the development of a new method for the identification of CD4+ T cells in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD4+, CD 8+, and B cell subsets are involved in the development and maintenance of distemper demyeilinating plaques.

the temporal and spatial distribution and density of CD4+, and CD8+ cells as well as the B cells in acute, subacute non-inflammatory, subacute inflammatory and in chronic plaques support the hypothesis of an immune mediated plaque pathogenesis.

the temporal and spatial distribution pattern of CD4+,CD8+, and B cell subsets and viral antigen in early and chronic lesions support the concept of heterogeneous in part immune mediated plaque pathogenesis in canine demyelinating distempered encephalitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDV is a major factor in the development of the disease and that the immune response to the virus is important in the development of demyelination.
the CD4+ and B cells are responsible for the plaque formation, whereas the CD8+ cells are involved in the viral clearance.
in the brain of distemper dogs, CD4+ and/or CD8+ cells as well as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity are involved in the pathogenesis of demyelination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD4+ T cell is the most important T cell subset in the pathogenesis of distemper encepha- litis.
the immune system plays a role in the development of demyelinating lesions.
the CD4 and CD 8 T cells as well a B cells are involved in the immune response in distemper.
